newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin appoints new foreign policy aide.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin appoints new foreign policy aide.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin appointed a new foreign affairs adviser on Wednesday in the latest of several changes to his foreign policy team, the Kremlin said in a statement.
Sergei Prikhodko, a 16-year Foreign Ministry veteran, was deputy director of the ministry's European department and before that deputy head of the Baltic countries section.
The Kremlin statement said Prikhodko, 40, had considerable experience in European affairs and spoke Czech, French and English.
Last Friday, Yeltsin also appointed his spokesman, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, 43, to coordinate foreign policy, and fired Dmitry Ryurikov, 50, his main foreign policy adviser.

Yastrzhembsky said the president was dissatisfied with Ryurikov's work on preparing documents related to a proposed Russian-Belarus union. Kremlin sources said Ryurikov pushed too hard for a rapid merger that was blocked by senior liberals.
